subject: Request: evidence for training exclusion, subprocessors, and ownership clarifications
messages:
From: security@stagemed.com
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: LLM training exclusion & subprocessor evidence

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week — StageMed's security team has a couple of follow-up asks before we can move to procurement:

1) A signed attestation we can present to our board that StageMed data will not be used to train or improve Redwood models (including any internal retraining pipelines).
2) A current list of subprocessors (and the regions they operate in).
3) Clarification on ownership for prompts and generated responses (we build embeddings and derivatives; need to ensure we retain rights).

We also need SOC 2 evidence and a suggested redline for our DPA if you have one. Can you point us to the right contacts and an estimated turnaround?

Thanks,
Security Team
StageMed Health

--
Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (PDF, 340KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: security@stagemed.com; Maya Singh <maya@stagemed.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: LLM training exclusion & subprocessor evidence

Hi Maya / StageMed security team,

Appreciate the thorough list. Looping in Rishi (legal) and Laura (privacy/compliance) — they will own the formal evidence and DPA redline. Quick answers up front so procurement has what it needs: 

- No-training commitment: We offer an explicit no-training (no-model-improvement) option for customer data by contract. That option prevents use of customer prompts/responses for any model training, evaluation, or tuning unless separately approved.

- Subprocessors: I'll attach our latest exported list and note the primary compute regions. If you need per-datacenter addresses we can provide that under an NDA.

- Ownership: By default, customers retain ownership of their prompts and outputs; Redwood provides the service to generate outputs and does not assert IP ownership over customer-supplied prompts or single-run generated content. If you plan to use outputs to build derived products (embeddings + fine-tuning), we can add explicit language to the DPA/SLA clarifying allowed uses and restrictions.

Next steps: Rishi will send a draft addendum covering a signed no-training attestation and suggested DPA redlines. Can procurement confirm target sign date? We can aim for a two-week turnaround on the contract if there are no major redlines.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attach: DPA_v3_redlined.pdf, subprocessor_list_2026-10.csv

--
Attachments: DPA_v3_redlined.pdf (PDF, 220KB); subprocessor_list_2026-10.csv (CSV, 18KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@stagemed.com>, security@stagemed.com
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: No-Training Addendum + DPA suggestions

Maya / StageMed team,

Thanks — please see the attached draft addendum that would be appended to our standard DPA. High-level points in the draft:

- No-Training Clause (proposed): Redwood agrees not to use Customer Data (defined as prompts, documents, outputs, embeddings) for model training, evaluation, or improvement unless the Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in. This includes offline experimentation, supervised fine-tuning, and metric collection for model updates.

- Logging & Retention: For customers who elect no-training, Redwood will still collect minimal operational logs (request IDs, timestamps, anonymized latency metrics) for reliability and billing. Customer data payloads will not be retained beyond configured retention windows (default 30 days) unless otherwise requested. If you require shorter retention, include desired windows and we will propose configuration + pricing.

- Subprocessors & Transfers: We provide a current subprocessor registry (attached) and commit to notifying you 30 days prior to adding new subprocessors. For cross-border transfers, we can offer EU-residency hosting or a VPC private deployment to keep all processing within chosen regions.

- Prompt/Response Ownership: Draft language clarifies that Customer retains all rights in prompts and outputs; Redwood asserts no ownership but reserves the right to use aggregated telemetry for platform health unless specifically excluded. The addendum includes an explicit carve-out for monitored, anonymized service telemetry.

I've prepared a redlined addendum (no-training-addendum-draft.docx) and a DocuSign envelope link for signature if the draft is acceptable: https://www.docusign.com/ENVELOPE/ABC123456789

If StageMed needs a signed attestation on company letterhead (for procurement/board), we can provide that after counter-signature.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: no-training-addendum-draft.docx (DOCX, 14KB)

From: Maya Singh <maya@stagemed.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stagemed.com, security@stagemed.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: No-Training Addendum + DPA suggestions

Thanks Rishi, Priya — this is very helpful. A couple of specific follow-ups before we route to procurement: 

1) Embeddings & Derivatives: If StageMed generates embeddings via the API and stores them in our data warehouse, can Redwood claim any rights over derivative models we build from those embeddings? We need a clear negative ("no rights granted to Redwood").

2) Logs accessible to support: Do Redwood engineers ever view raw prompt/response content during troubleshooting? We can tolerate redacted excerpts with approval, but need a process.

3) Evidence: Would you be able to provide a signed attestation (PDF) on Redwood letterhead confirming the no-training commitment once the addendum is finalized? Procurement will want that as part of our package.

Also attaching our procurement checklist for reference. If you can send a DocuSign when the addendum is ready we can prioritize review.

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of Security Operations | StageMed Health

--
Attachment: procurement-checklist.pdf (PDF, 120KB); SOC2-summary.pdf (from earlier)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@stagemed.com>, procurement@stagemed.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: No-Training Addendum + DPA suggestions

Maya — thanks for the clear questions. Quick commitments and next steps: 

- Embeddings/Derivatives: Confirmed — Redwood does not claim ownership or IP rights over embeddings or derivative models you build from customer data. We'll add an explicit negative statement to the addendum.

- Support access to raw content: Engineers do not proactively review raw prompt/response content. For troubleshooting, we can produce redacted excerpts or require joint remote sessions where StageMed can redact sensitive fields before sharing. Any ad-hoc access will require written approval and will be logged; we can add that workflow to the SLA.

- Signed attestation: Yes — once the addendum is countersigned we will provide a signed attestation PDF on Redwood letterhead for procurement and board use.

Plan: Rishi will upload the final addendum to DocuSign by end of day tomorrow with the negative-ownership clause and the support-access workflow. Priya will coordinate a 2-week MSA/DPA review window with procurement and provide the signed attestation after signature.

If StageMed wants to avoid cross-border transfer risks entirely, we can propose a Private (VPC) deployment quote; happy to connect with solutions engineering if useful.

Thanks — I'll send the DocuSign link when ready.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

--
Action items: Rishi to finalize addendum; Priya to send DocuSign link; StageMed to confirm procurement timeline.
